rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the difference by context: al-Shura discusses earthly provision and people, while al-Ankabut calls people to reflect on creation; Hud addresses the afterlife and reckoning of earth's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: الكلام في سورة هود متعلق بالآخرة وبمحاسبة أهل الأرض أما السياق في سورة الشورى ففي الكلام على نعم الله تعالى في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unusual order in 29:64 puts distraction before play because wealth and provision occasion diversion, as in the warning not to let wealth and children distract believers.
rows.anchor: فالرزق ليس مدعاة اللعب وإنما مدعاة اللهو كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 17:96, God's attributes close the verse, so “witness” comes first; in 29:52, the closing judgment concerns people, so “between me and you” comes first.
rows.anchor: لذا اقتضى تقديم ما يتعلّق بالبشر (بيني وبينكم) على (شهيدا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted specification broadens the question to include everything God promised, to the disbelievers and others, including resurrection and judgment; Quraysh believed in God but denied the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إذن الحذف هنا أدى إلى توسع في المعنى لأنه شمل ما وعدهم ووعد غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “bi-mā tuʾmar,” mā can be a verbal noun (“our command”) or a relative pronoun (“what you are commanded”); omitting bihi preserves both readings.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحذف هنا يدل على التوسع في المعنى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: One reported interpretation attaches “without reckoning” to the reward: it is poured out abundantly, emphasizing the great measure of the reward.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون يفسرونها أحد تفسيرين: إما أن الأجر يُصبّ عليهم صباً بغير حساب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The other interpretation attaches the phrase to the patient: they receive reward without being called to account, with their sins forgiven and Paradise granted without reckoning.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون يفسرونها أحد تفسيرين: إما أن الأجر يُصبّ عليهم صباً بغير حساب للدلالة على المبالغة في الأجر، أو أن الصابرين يصب عليهم الأجر ولا يحاسبون

rows.speaker: رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The cited hadith says that seventy thousand from the Prophet's community will enter Paradise without reckoning; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الشريف عن سول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:"سبعون ألفاً من أمتي يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 42:28, despair during withheld rain comes before rain as mercy: enduring drought calls for patience, then rain calls for gratitude, explaining why patience precedes thanks.
rows.anchor: الأول (القنوط) يحتاج إلى صبر والثاني (إنزال الغيث) يحتاج إلى الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships left motionless when God stills the wind present a hardship requiring patience.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر يحتاج إلى الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading of “destroy them” uses a metonymy of place for those aboard: it is the people in the ships who perish, a calamity requiring patience.
rows.anchor: احتمال إرادة إهلاك من فيها، على المجاز المرسل، فأطلق المحل وأراد الحالّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is destruction of the ships or their cargo, a loss of property; either this or the loss of lives requires patience, while God's pardon calls for thanks.
rows.anchor: أو احتمال إرادة البضائع التي فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding examples repeatedly call for patience through hardship and gratitude for mercy and pardon, making the ending “patient, grateful” fit the context.
rows.anchor: ما تقدّم الآية موضع السؤال وما جاء بعدها يحتاج لصبر وشكر والصبر تقدّم على الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min in “min qablika” marks a starting point immediately before the Prophet's time and an unbroken span reaching back to Adam.
rows.anchor: وذكر (من) تفيد الابتداء أي ابتداء الغاية وهو امتداد من الزمن الذي قبلك مباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without min, “before you” can refer either to the near past or to a more distant past.
rows.anchor: وهي تحتمل البعيد والقريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in phrases such as “from above their heads” and “around the Throne” signals no intervening gap; by contrast, 44:48's wording describes a lighter punishment.
rows.anchor: أي ليس هناك فاصل بين الرأس والصبّ حتى لا تضيع أية حرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice to include min follows context: it suits an extended chain of events or prophets, while its omission suits a limited period or a context focused on preaching.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان السياق ممتد يأتي بـ (من) وإذا كان السياق لفترة محددة لا يأتي بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the negative particle before both verbs excludes both joint and separate instances of error and delusion; the Prophet is guided and rightly directed.
rows.anchor: وهذا حتى لا يتصور أنه نفى الجمع بينهما فقط وإنما نفى الجمع بينهما والإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating past error means he was never astray; affirmative “he was guided” might suggest a limited period or that he had been astray before guidance.
rows.anchor: مهتد رشيد لم يسبق له ضلالة في أي وقت وزمن كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense negation covers the Prophet's speech now and in the future, unlike a past-tense form; ʿan marks motive or source, declaring his speech's motive pure as well as its content truthful.
rows.anchor: بتزكية الدافع للقول فالدافع له زكي صادق ونطقه صادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirya is doubt or casting suspicion, unlike argument over ideas: the disbelievers challenged the report, not the vision itself, so the verse says not to dispute what he sees.
rows.anchor: فالكفار كانوا يشككون في الرواية وليس في الأفكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of ʿalā with the vision contrasts with fī in the previous verse: the vision itself is not the subject of dispute, unlike reports about the unseen Hour.
rows.anchor: والملاحظ هنا استخدام حرف (على) أما في الآية السابقة استخدم الحرف (في)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazla, from descending, is more specific than marra: Muhammad saw Gabriel on his descent back, after ascending above the place Gabriel could reach.
rows.anchor: استخدم كلمة نزلة وليس كلمة (مرة) لأن النزلة من النزول فقال ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: The author cites Gabriel telling the Prophet to proceed and saying that he would have been burned had he advanced farther, as support for the Prophet's greater ascent.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل - عليه السلام - قال للرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - تقدم وقال لو تقدمتُ لاحترقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muntahā means the last or furthest point, which is located by the Garden of Abode.
rows.anchor: المنتهى هي آخر شيء وآخر نقطة ومكانها عند جنة المأوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things that covered the Lote Tree and what the Prophet saw during this journey are matters beyond our knowledge; God knows their reality.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية أمور لا نعرفها نحن فالله أعلم بمجريات هذه الرحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David's Psalms are singled out because they were revealed in installments, like the Qur'an; this reminds disbelievers who accept David that Muhammad too received a scripture.
rows.anchor: لأن الزبور نزل منجما أي بالتقسيط كما أنزل القرآن على الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage argues that Muhammad received revelation just as Noah and the other prophets did, and that God sent him as a messenger just as He sent them; this answers disbelievers who accept earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: وتؤمنون بالأنبياء الذين أوحينا إليهم وقد أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى باقي الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spoke to Moses at the sacred valley and on Sinai, the highest place Moses reached; Muhammad ascended to the higher Sidrat al-Muntaha, so God gave him the grounds for belief and removed the disbelievers' objection.
rows.anchor: وأعلى مكان كلّم الله تعالى موسى عليه هو الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite “the right” refers to a particular justification for killing; the indefinite “any right” denies any justification, and is used to stress aggression.
rows.anchor: فإذا أراد تعالى أن يبين لنا العدوان يذكر (بغير حق)

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi distinguishes al-nabiyyīn as a description of those being informed from al-anbiyāʾ as the plural of prophet after becoming one; the author adds “God knows best.”
rows.anchor: ويقول الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي عن معنى كلمة النبيين والأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inzāl is used for scripture sent down, whereas ītāʾ can apply to scriptures and other gifts, such as miracles, and is therefore broader.
rows.anchor: أما الإيتاء فهو يستعمل للكتب وغير الكتب مثل المعجزات والإيتاء أوسع من الإنزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses received miracles before receiving scripture; the Qur'an never says scripture was “sent down” to Moses, using ūtia for him, while both ūtia and inzāl are used for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لم يرد في القرآن كلمة (أنزل) مطلقا لموسى في القرآن كله وإنما استعملت كلمة (أوتي) لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says repetition can emphasize: the refrain occurs seven times in the Hell material, matching Hell's seven gates, and eight times in the Paradise material, matching Paradise's eight gates.
rows.anchor: تكرار الآيات قد يكون للتوكيد ففي ذكر النار من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators identify the dual addressees of the refrain as the two accountable groups, humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: ويقول المفسرون أن المقصود بهما الثقلان أي الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say direct address does not require a preceding address; one can ask a group a question even without prior speech to them.
rows.anchor: يقول عامة المفسرون أنه ليس بالضرورة عندما تخاطب واحدا أو جماعة أن يسبقه كلام

rows.speaker: قسم من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators restrict al-anām, the earthly inhabitants, to the two groups of humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: وقسم من المفسرين يحصرونها بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: قسم آخر من المفسرين
rows.claim: Other commentators take al-anām to mean all creatures on earth; the author says this sense still includes humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: وقسم آخر يقول: أنها تعني كل المخلوقات على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the refrain, the surah has already commanded the accountable humans and jinn about justice in weighing and taught them the Qur'an; the address therefore follows established context.
rows.anchor: قبل الآية الأولى فيها خطاب المكلفين وهما الإنس والجن

none: Question only; the answer is in the next segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is named before human creation because it is the book of worship, and worship is the purpose for which humans and jinn were created; purpose precedes the work it governs.
rows.anchor: فلما كان خلق الإنسان والجن لغرض العبادة والقرآن هو كتاب العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an, as God's speech and part of His knowledge, already existed before the human being; it thus precedes creation in existence as well as purpose.
rows.anchor: القرآن كلام الله ومن علم الله وهو موجود قبل الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is prior in purpose, existence, and merit; Qur'anic order need not be chronological and may instead follow context, priority, or excellence, sometimes placing a later event first.
rows.anchor: إذا كان على الفضل هو أسبق وإذا كان على الزمن هو أسبق وإذا كان على العلة والغرض هو أسبق
